summary: Mexico's National Migration Institute (INM) publishes a list of countries and regions whose nationals do not need a visa to travel to Mexico as visitors without permission to do paid work (tourism), and says a visitor cannot exceed 180 days. A valid visa from Canada, the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom or any Schengen country can be presented as an alternative to the Mexican visa, and a free electronic authorization (SAE) lets nationals of Ukraine, Turkey and Russia travel to Mexico by air without a paper visa.

quote.text: El Sistema de Autorización Electrónica -o visa electrónica- es un mecanismo que se aplica a los nacionales de Ucrania, Turquía y Rusia, con objeto de viajar a México, por vía aérea, sin necesidad de obtener una visa en papel en la Embajada de México correspondiente, bajo la condición de estancia de visitante sin permiso para realizar actividades remuneradas, con motivos turísticos, tránsito por México, negocios (asistencia a juntas, visitas de supervisión, capacitación o asesorías en México), actividades relacionadas con el ejercicio de los ministros de culto, trabajos técnicos en empresas (sin recibir pago en México), actividades filantrópicas, deportivas, transporte de mercancías, recibir tratamientos médicos, asistir a ferias o conferencias, además de realización de estudios que no impliquen una remuneración en México y que la temporalidad de la visita no sea mayor a 180 días.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Mexico?
faq.answer: No. INM's list of countries and regions whose nationals do not need a visa to travel to Mexico includes the United States of America, and INM says a visitor cannot exceed 180 days. Canada's travel advice says that if you enter by air, an immigration official will stamp your passport and note the number of days you are allowed to stay.

faq.question: I have a US visa — do I still need a Mexican visa?
faq.answer: No. INM lists a valid visa from Canada, the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom or any Schengen country among the documents a foreign national can present as an alternative to the Mexican visa, and says a visitor cannot exceed 180 days.

faq.question: Is the FMM tourist card still required?
faq.answer: Only if you enter by land: INM requires a completed FMM for land entries, and says that at international airports you do not have to present, fill in or carry an FMM, as it is generated at entry and your entry stamp carries the necessary information. Canada's travel advice says air arrivals need to complete a Multiple Digital Migratory Form (FMMD) online upon arrival and keep a copy.

faq.question: What is Mexico's SAE electronic authorization?
faq.answer: The SAE (Sistema de Autorización Electrónica, or electronic visa) lets nationals of Ukraine, Turkey and Russia travel to Mexico by air without obtaining a paper visa from the Mexican embassy. It is free, granted for one trip with one entry and a stay of up to 180 days, and the approved application is valid for 30 days to travel and enter Mexico.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Mexico as a tourist?
faq.answer: INM says a visitor cannot exceed 180 days. Canada's travel advice says that if you enter by air, an immigration official will stamp your passport and note the number of days you are allowed to stay in Mexico.

Most foreign visitors must pay a migratory entry fee.

This fee is normally included in airline and cruise ship tickets. Foreign visitors arriving by land will have to pay this fee at the migration entry booth with a credit or debit card, at a bank following entry, or online prior to arrival. The receipt must be attached to your FMM for submission at departure.
You don’t have to pay this fee if you’re entering by land for tourism purposes and your stay will not exceed 7 days.

levies.exemptions: The Canadian government says visitors entering by land for tourism whose stay will not exceed 7 days do not pay it.
levies.text: The INM fee table charges MXN 983 for the receipt, review and issue of the migration document of a visitor without permission for paid activities (DNR). The Canadian government says most foreign visitors must pay this migratory entry fee and that it is normally included in airline and cruise ship tickets. It says visitors arriving by land pay at the migration entry booth by card, at a bank after entry or online before arrival, and that visitors entering by land for tourism for no more than 7 days do not pay it.
